articles.title: En los años 80, Vicente Fernández adquirió 500 hectáreas en Jalisco; convirtió el terreno en un rancho con caballerizas y una arena para miles de personas
articles.standfirst: Vicente Fernández construyó el Rancho Los Tres Potrillos.
articles.summary: Vicente Fernández construyó el Rancho Los Tres Potrillos.
articles.body: Vicente Fernández fue uno de los cantantes más influyentes de México, especialmente para el género ranchero pues su éxito se mantuvo por décadas, lo que lo convirtió en toda una leyenda en nuestro país. Fue tal el poder éconómico que tuvo, que en la década de los 80 pudo comprar un terreno de 500 hectáreas, donde edificó el icónico rancho Los Tres Potrillos. El rancho Los Tres Potrillos es uno de los lugares más emblemáticos relacionados con la vida de Vicente Fernández, conocido como El Charro de Huentitán y El Rey de la Música Ranchera. Ubicado en el estado de Jalisco, cerca de Guadalajara, este extenso terreno fue el hogar del cantante durante buena parte de su vida y un espacio donde convivían su familia, su pasión por los caballos y su amor por las tradiciones mexicanas. El lugar recibió su nombre en honor a sus tres hijos varones: Vicente Fernández Jr., Gerardo Fernández y Alejandro Fernández. Con el paso de los años, se convirtió en un símbolo de la dinastía Fernández y en un sitio estrechamente ligado a la imagen pública del intérprete de canciones como El Rey, Volver, volver y Por tu maldito amor. A continuación en MARCA MX te contamos más sobre este lugar. Los Tres Potrillos destaca por su ambiente campirano, sus instalaciones ecuestres y los elementos decorativos que reflejan la identidad charra de Vicente Fernández. No se trata únicamente de una residencia, sino de una propiedad vinculada con los caballos, la música ranchera y la vida familiar del cantante. Entre sus características más conocidas se encuentran: El rancho también fue importante para el trabajo del cantante. Allí podía descansar lejos de los escenarios, convivir con sus seres queridos y mantenerse cerca de las actividades que disfrutaba fuera de la música. La propiedad representaba, además, el resultado de una trayectoria artística que lo llevó de presentarse en lugares modestos a convertirse en una de las figuras más reconocidas de la música mexicana. Por su relación con la historia de Vicente Fernández, Los Tres Potrillos se transformó en un sitio de interés para sus seguidores. Sin embargo, conviene distinguir entre la fama del rancho y el acceso a sus distintas áreas: las condiciones de visita pueden variar y no debe darse por hecho que toda la propiedad privada está abierta al público. El nombre de Los Tres Potrillos permanece ligado al legado de Chente. Más que una residencia famosa, representa una parte de su historia personal, su vínculo con Jalisco y la tradición ranchera que defendió durante décadas. Vicente Fernández Gómez nació el 17 de febrero de 1940 en Huentitán El Alto, Jalisco. Fue cantante, actor y productor, y se convirtió en uno de los máximos exponentes de la música ranchera y del mariachi. Su estilo interpretativo, su potente voz y su característica vestimenta de charro lo hicieron reconocible en México y en numerosos países de habla hispana. Entre sus canciones más recordadas figuran Volver, volver, El Rey, Mujeres divinas, Por tu maldito amor, Acá entre nos y De qué manera te olvido. Su repertorio ayudó a mantener vigente la música ranchera y a acercarla a nuevas generaciones de público. Vicente Fernández falleció el 12 de diciembre de 2021, a los 81 años, en Guadalajara, Jalisco. Su muerte provocó muestras de duelo entre admiradores, músicos y figuras públicas. Fue sepultado en el rancho Los Tres Potrillos, un lugar que adquirió todavía mayor significado para sus seguidores tras su fallecimiento.

articles.title: Alfredo Adame con un pie en prisión: Gustavo Adolfo Infante pide varios años en la cárcel para el actor y conductor
articles.standfirst: Un juez declaró culpable a Alfredo Adame por discriminación en agravio de la madre de Gustavo Adolfo Infante
articles.summary: Un juez declaró culpable a Alfredo Adame por discriminación en agravio de la madre de Gustavo Adolfo Infante
articles.body: El enfrentamiento entre Alfredo Adame y Gustavo Adolfo Infante dio un giro serio. Luego de que un juez del Poder Judicial de la Ciudad de México declarara culpable al actor por el delito de discriminación, este jueves 15 de octubre se programó la audiencia para individualizar la sanción. Infante y su equipo legal buscan una condena de hasta tres años de prisión, mientras Adame restó importancia al fallo y aseguró que no teme ir a la cárcel. El origen del conflicto se remonta a 2022. En ese entonces, Adame lanzó declaraciones públicas contra Elvia Inés Seañez, madre del periodista, a quien acusó de practicar “magia negra”, de estar involucrada en robos y de otras conductas ilícitas. Infante tomó el caso como una ofensa grave y presentó la denuncia por discriminación. Tras casi cuatro años de proceso, el juez determinó que Adame era culpable. El actor no se guardó nada. Calificó la resolución de “aberración” y dijo no creer en la justicia. “El juez me la receta, soy culpable. No es de morirse, no es de cárcel… puede que sus abogados pidan un año de cárcel, tres años de cárcel, se conmuta una multa, pagar 16 mil 800 pesos del psicólogo y a lo mejor trabajo social, no sé, no pasa nada”, declaró. Anunció que apelará de inmediato, argumentando que no se trata de un delito grave. Según el Código Penal de la Ciudad de México, el delito de discriminación contempla penas de uno a tres años de prisión, trabajo comunitario y multa. La sentencia definitiva se define precisamente en la audiencia de individualización de la pena. Gustavo Adolfo Infante no se conforma con esta sentencia. Ya anunció que presentará dos demandas civiles más por daño moral: una por las afectaciones a su madre y otra por las expresiones dirigidas contra él. El periodista ha mantenido una postura firme desde el inicio y ha convertido el caso en una de las batallas legales más mediáticas del espectáculo mexicano. Mientras tanto, en redes sociales el tema volvió a encenderse este jueves. Publicaciones recientes señalan que Infante “quiere meter a la cárcel a Adame” y que busca los tres años de prisión. Adame, por su parte, sigue restándole gravedad y confía en que la pena se conmute o se reduzca a una sanción económica y trabajo social. El desenlace aún está por escribirse. Lo que sí quedó claro es que el viejo rencor entre el actor y el periodista sigue vivo, y esta vez la justicia mexicana tiene la última palabra.

articles.title: Aumento salarial del IMSS 2027: Cuánto piden los trabajadores y por qué rechazan la propuesta
articles.standfirst: El aumento salarial del IMSS 2027 fue rechazado por los trabajadores. Conoce cuánto ofrecieron, cuánto piden y cuáles son sus principales demandas
articles.summary: El aumento salarial del IMSS 2027 fue rechazado por los trabajadores. Conoce cuánto ofrecieron, cuánto piden y cuáles son sus principales demandas
articles.body: La negociación salarial del IMSS para 2026-2027 quedó nuevamente sobre la mesa después de que miles de trabajadores salieran a las calles y posteriormente rechazaran en consulta el convenio alcanzado entre el instituto y su sindicato. Aunque la propuesta representaba un aumento global de 6.8%, la cifra no convenció a la mayoría de quienes participaron en la votación. El rechazo abrió una nueva etapa de negociaciones. La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum informó que el director general del IMSS, Zoé Robledo, revisará alternativas para presentar una nueva propuesta que otorgue mayores beneficios a los trabajadores. Pero ¿cuánto representa realmente el incremento ofrecido y qué están exigiendo quienes laboran en el Seguro Social? El convenio sometido a consulta contemplaba un incremento global de 6.8%, aunque no todo correspondía directamente al salario. La propuesta para los trabajadores del IMSS se dividía de la siguiente manera: La consulta se realizó el miércoles 14 de octubre y estuvo dirigida a un padrón de 476 mil 260 trabajadores en activo, con cerca de 670 puntos de votación en todo el país. Un corte preliminar reportó alrededor de 282 mil participantes hasta las 19:00 horas, equivalentes a cerca de 60% del padrón. Finalmente, la mayoría decidió rechazar el convenio. Para una parte de la base trabajadora del IMSS, el incremento directo al salario resultó insuficiente frente a las condiciones laborales que enfrentan. El rechazo ocurrió además después de una movilización en la Ciudad de México en la que participaron trabajadores activos y jubilados. Entre las principales inconformidades estuvieron: Una trabajadora señaló que, en su caso, el incremento representaría apenas 107 pesos por quincena, de los cuales 40 se destinarían a la Afore. Las demandas van más allá del salario. Durante las movilizaciones, los trabajadores del IMSS también plantearon que el presupuesto destinado a salud represente al menos 7% del PIB y pidieron modificaciones a la Ley del Seguro Social para garantizar la viabilidad financiera del instituto. También denunciaron carencias de insumos, medicamentos y personal. Un trabajador señaló que en algunas unidades deben atender a numerosos pacientes durante turnos prolongados sin contar con materiales suficientes. Por ahora, no existe un nuevo porcentaje salarial confirmado. Sheinbaum señaló que Zoé Robledo deberá revisar las alternativas “en el marco de lo posible”, mientras el SNTSS analiza la continuidad de las negociaciones. La siguiente propuesta será clave: el conflicto podría encaminarse hacia un acuerdo si incorpora tanto una mejora salarial como respuestas a las condiciones laborales, pero los trabajadores del IMSS ya advirtieron que su movimiento apenas comienza.

articles.title: Gala Montes revela el hiriente mensaje que su mamá le escribió cuando era niña
articles.standfirst: La artista mexicana contó una triste anécdota en su juventud
articles.summary: La artista mexicana contó una triste anécdota en su juventud
articles.body: En las últimas semanas, Gala Montes ha estado involucrada en una serie de polémicas que han acaparado la atención de la opinión pública. Sin embargo, su último posteo en Instagram ha causado empatía con la artista, quien aprovechó las redes sociales para exponer su corazón y sus sentimientos. La actriz y cantante aprovechó las redes sociales para evidenciar a su madre, Crista Montes, con quien se ha alejado tras una difícil relación familiar desatado desde hace un par de años tras conflictos por el modo en el que manejó su carrera artística cuando era una niña. Ahora, Gala compartió una fotografía que contiene un mensaje que, según expuso, le escribió su madre y el cual fue muy hiriente en su momento y ha abierto una vieja herida que aún duele. En su cuenta pública de Instagram, Gala Montes posteo una fotografía suya de su infancia y el cual contenía un mensaje escrito en pluma, y asegura que fue redactado por su propia madre. Junto a la publicación, la actriz reconoció que intentó grabar un video para explicar lo que sentía, pero no pudo hacerlo debido a la tristeza que le provocó recordar el episodio. La también solista habló del dolor que le provoca recordar esas palabras y explicó que su nuevo proyecto musical, "La Hija de Nadie", busca acompañar a quienes han sentido que no pertenecen a ningún lugar. “Quería hacer un video explicando pero además de que se me cortaba la voz, no hay nada que explicar sin embargo mucha gente juzga mis pies y me duele demasiado porque no saben lo difícil que es que tu mamá te escriba esto”, expresó en redes sociales. Gala Montes hizo público el distanciamiento con su madre el 9 de julio de 2024, durante una transmisión en vivo en redes sociales cuando Crista ofrecía una entrevista para la revista TVNotas, en la que aseguró que su hija la había despedido injustamente como su representante. Tras el distanciamiento con su madre, expuesto hace un par de años, previo a su entrada a "La casa de los famosos México", Montes también se ha distanciado de su hermana y su sobrina; públicamente ha hablado sobre su consumo de mariguana, lo que la ha puesto en el centro de la polémica por ciertos comportamientos y declaraciones. Tras la entrevista de Crista con la revista de espectáculos, Gala denunció presuntos episodios de manipulación, violencia, extorsión y despojo económico que, según su testimonio, habría vivido desde niña por explotación laboral que habría experimentado desde los seis años, fue hasta el 9 de septiembre de 2026 cuando llamó directamente a su madre “explotadora infantil”, y lo hizo mediante una publicación en redes sociales en la que reclamó: “YA PÁGAME EL ANEXO Y TODO LO QUE ME DEBES EXPLOTADORA INFANTIL”.

articles.title: Dylan Garand Responds to Adversity With Strong Showing In Rangers' Loss To Blue Jackets
articles.summary: Dylan Garand’s 28-save performance wasn't enough to secure a victory on Saturday night, as the New York Rangers lost 1-0 to the Columbus Blue Jackets in over...
articles.body:
Dylan Garand's 28-save performance wasn't enough to secure a victory on Saturday night, as the New York Rangers lost 1-0 to the Columbus Blue Jackets in overtime, but any concerns about Garand's shaky performance against the New Jersey Devils on Thursday night were put to rest.

The Rangers' 7-1 loss to the Devils on Thursday night reached a low point in the second period, as Garand was pulled for the first time in his NHL career after giving up four goals on 13 shots, including three goals in the span of less than five minutes.

For the first time since taking over the starting goaltending job from Igor Shesterkin in the wake of his season-ending injury, Garand, who had come into New Jersey with a 5-1-1 record, .949 save percentage, and 1.37 GAA across his seven NHL games, looked rattled, with the implications of Shesterkin's injury truly setting in.

As a team, the Rangers stuck by the rookie goaltender and went right back to him on Saturday night in Columbus.

"I knew he was going to bounce back tonight," Sullivan said. "I said that to him before the game. I knew he was going to be good."

The 24-year-old goalie set the tone early in the contest with a pad save on Adam Fantilli, and his play only grew from there.

Throughout the night, Garand was composed in his net. He was aggressive yet positionally sound when Columbus had its scoring opportunities.

The game was relatively even, with both teams attempting 29 shots on net and trading three power-play opportunities without a goal on either side.

When the Rangers needed Garand to make timely saves, he delivered, highlighted by a diving glove save on Cole Sillinger toward the end of the third period and a glove save in overtime with Sean Monahan taking a shot from the doorstep of the net.

"It was a huge response," Sullivan said. "He was solid in there. He has a quiet confidence about him. I thought he made timely saves for us. I thought he was real good."

The Rangers were unable to come up with the win in Columbus, as they failed to convert on three power-play tries in the third period and gave up a goal late in the overtime frame, courtesy of Kent Johnson.

Regardless of the loss, Garand showed his strong mental toughness for a young goaltender and his ability to bounce back after what was his worst NHL performance.

"Games like that happen," Garand said. "The best goalies in the world: Carey Price, Henrik Lundqvist, Igor, everyone's been pulled, that happens. I think you just learn from it and move on. I don't think a lot of us like the way we played that game. And myself personally, I wasn't happy. I don't think I did a good enough job of being present, and maybe let the self-doubt a little bit creep in too much to my game. It doesn't change my capability when games like that happen so just trust in myself trust in my game and respond."

The Rangers recently added veteran goaltender James Reimer to their American Hockey League pipeline, but that addition likely doesn't change the fact that the Blueshirts will need Garand to take on a bulk of the starts for the foreseeable future, at least until Joonas Korpisalo is activated from injured reserve, which is expected to happen in a few weeks.

Garand has started in all four games since Shesterkin went down with a season-ending lower-body injury, and Sullivan has continued to show trust in Garand through both his words and actions, which should only continue moving forward.

"I just think it speaks volumes for his character," Sullivan said of Garand's performance against the Blue Jackets. "He's a high-character kid. I said that after the Jersey game. I mean it…

"It's just part of his makeup. He's a competitive guy. He's got a lot of pride in his game. He knows how important he is to helping this team win, and he's trying to take advantage of the opportunity that he has. So I was happy for him, but it didn't surprise me."

articles.title: FSU football grades: Mike Norvell leads Seminoles to solid effort, tough loss
articles.summary: The Florida State Seminoles took Miami to the brink, but a double-overtime defeat leaves FSU wondering what could've been.
articles.body:
Florida State had every opportunity to snap its road losing streak and pull off a season-defining upset Saturday night.

Instead, the Seminoles watched a valiant effort end in heartbreak, falling 43-35 to rival Miami in double overtime despite multiple chances to seize control of the game.

The loss drops FSU to 3-4 overall and 1-3 in ACC play, adding further pressure to a season that continues to raise questions about coach Mike Norvell's future. Here's how the Seminoles graded out after their latest setback.

FSU football vs Miami Hurricanes: Photos from ACC rivalry game

Daniels turned in one of his most efficient performances of the season, completing 15 of 26 passes for 298 yards and four touchdowns.

The senior showed poise throughout the night and delivered several key deep throws, particularly in the second half, helping keep Florida State within striking distance against one of the conference's top teams. He also battled through constant pressure as Miami limited his ability to impact the game with his legs.

The performance wasn't flawless. There were still moments when Daniels appeared hesitant to trust what he saw downfield, and his final desperation pass intended for Duce Robinson was intercepted, ending any hopes of a miracle finish. Still, Daniels demonstrated toughness and leadership while giving the Seminoles a chance to win until the final play.

FSU offense faced a significant challenge when running back Ousmane Kromah exited late in the second quarter.

Tre Wisner stepped up admirably, scoring on a screen pass that gave FSU its first lead of the night at 21-14 in the third quarter. Wisner finished with four catches for 56 yards and added 34 rushing yards on seven carries. However, his fourth-quarter fumble in a tie game proved costly.

The Seminoles were slow to involve some of their biggest playmakers. Robinson didn't emerge as a major factor until late in regulation but still finished with 113 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including several clutch catches. Desirro Riles added his first touchdown of the season, while Jayvann Boggs and Jasen Lopez also contributed.

Despite the production, FSU lacked consistency for long stretches and struggled to fully capitalize on favorable opportunities against Miami's defense.

The final score may not reflect it, but FSU's defense did enough at times to keep the Seminoles in contention deep into the game.

Facing Miami's explosive offense, the Seminoles generated pressure with their front four and forced quarterback Darian Mensah into his first interception of the game during the third quarter. The defense also recorded a sack and repeatedly disrupted the Hurricanes ' rhythm.

Chris Jones delivered one of the game's biggest moments, stopping Miami on a fourth-and-short attempt for the third consecutive week in a critical short-yardage situation.

Still, FSU had no answer for Miami's top playmakers. Malachi Toney finished with 10 catches for 151 yards and a touchdown, while Javian Mallory rushed for 108 yards and two scores. The inability to slow either player ultimately proved too much to overcome.

Given the wet conditions and slick football, punter Daniels Hughes provided a steady performance.

Hughes placed two punts inside the 20-yard line and helped limit opportunities for Miami's dangerous return game. It wasn't a flashy night for the special teams unit, but it was a dependable one.

FSU's effort and preparation kept the Seminoles competitive for all four quarters and two overtime periods. The players continued to fight until the final whistle, reflecting positively on Norvell and his staff.

However, the game once again spotlighted several critical fourth-down decisions. FSU failed on two goal-line attempts, leaving points on the field in a game ultimately decided by one possession. Similar questions emerged after the Louisville loss, and those missed opportunities loomed large as the Seminoles pursued a marquee victory.

Aside from those decisions, the coaching staff devised a strong game plan that put FSU in position to win. Unfortunately, a handful of costly choices and missed opportunities overshadowed much of the night's positive work.

FSU's performance was good enough to threaten one of the ACC's top teams on the road, but not good enough to finish the job.

The Seminoles showed resilience, received one of Daniels' best performances of the season and battled a rival into double overtime. Yet untimely turnovers, missed opportunities in key situations and defensive breakdowns against Miami's stars prevented Florida State from securing what would have been its biggest win of the year.

In the end, the effort was encouraging. The result, however, was another painful loss in a season running out of opportunities for moral victories.

articles.title: Burns, Chalk leave marks in Southern Utah's 38-17 win over UC Davis
articles.summary: CEDAR CITY, Utah (AP) — Quarterback Will Burns accounted for four total touchdowns and Floyd Chalk ran for a career-high 212 yards and Southern Utah used the...
articles.body:
CEDAR CITY, Utah (AP) — Quarterback Will Burns accounted for four total touchdowns and Floyd Chalk ran for a career-high 212 yards and Southern Utah used the second half to overpower UC Davis 38-17 on Saturday.

Burns was 13-of-20 passing for just 126 yards but had two touchdowns. On the ground, Burns ran for 98 yards on 11 carries and reached the end zone twice.

Chalk had a touchdown on his 26 carries as he bested his previous career-high 183 yards rushing set on Sept. 5 in a 47-42 win over Weber State.

Trailing 17-9 at halftime, Burns led a 13-play, 73-yard scoring drive that lasted eight minutes. It ended with his 1-yard pass to Joshua Accord. Burns ran it in for the two-point conversion to tie it.

Three minutes later, Burns threw a 6-yard touchdown to Accord and the Thunderbirds (3-4, 2-2) led for the remainder.

Nate Dahle threw for 282 yards, two touchdowns and an interception for UC Davis (4-3, 2-2) which entered as the 14th-ranked team in the Stats Perform FCS Top 25 poll.

UC Davis host Northern Colorado on Saturday.

Southern Utah travels to face Idaho on Saturday.

articles.title: Watch: FSU loses to Miami in overtime after controversial calls
articles.summary: The FSU Seminoles lost to the Miami Hurricanes in double overtime with controversial calls on several plays. Take a look at them here.
articles.body:
The FSU Seminoles lost to the Miami Hurricanes 43-35 on Saturday in Hard Rock Stadium, with the game going into double overtime. While every loss stings, this one hurt even more due to the two controversial calls that went against FSU.

The teams traded touchdowns in the first overtime before Miami scored to start the second overtime, completing a pass to Malachi Toney, who then completed a pass on a trick play to put them up by eight. The Seminoles were quickly in trouble, with Ashton Daniels getting sacked on first down before throwing an incomplete pass on second and 16. A false start on Quintrevion Wisner made it 3rd and 21, with another incompletion setting up 4th and 21.

With the game on the line, FSU took its final timeout to get ready, with Mike Norvell trying to dial up a heroic play. He did just that, with Micahi Danzy getting open and Daniels finding him for the touchdown. However, the refs called a questionable holding penalty on Xavier Chaplin, wiping out the touchdown and setting up 4th and 31. You can see the hold here.

With FSU backed up even further, Daniels heaved it to Duce Robinson in the end zone, who was in a great spot to make a play and seemingly did so, but the ref ruled that the Miami defensive back came down with the game-ending interception, confirming the call with replay.

It was another close call, which once again went against FSU and drew the ire of their fans . Here is a look at the final play.

articles.title: It’s Time for Oklahoma to Move On From John Mateer
articles.summary: A catastrophic three-turnover collapse against Kentucky proves the Red River hero lacks the ball security to lead Norman’s offense. Reliable production must...
articles.body:
One week after the Red River high, John Mateer just reminded everybody why this offense still cannot be trusted. Oklahoma l ost 21-13 to Kentucky at home , and while the final score will get filed under another frustrating SEC night, the bigger issue is simpler: Mateer is not the answer.

Not for the rest of this season, and not as the bridge into whatever comes next.

He had his moment in Dallas. He made the throws to Isaiah Sategna, managed the game well enough, and got to be the quarterback who helped end the Texas drought. That was real. It was also not enough to paper over everything else.

Against Kentucky, Mateer threw for 270 yards and still walked out as the biggest reason Oklahoma lost a game it had every chance to win. Three turnovers. Two of them in the worst possible moments. A pick-six that ended the night.

The season-long number is even uglier. Mateer now has 10 total turnovers through six games. He entered Saturday with four interceptions and three lost fumbles. Then he added three more turnovers against Kentucky, all in the second half.

At some point, production stops mattering if the ball keeps hitting the ground or landing in the other team's hands. Oklahoma can talk about toughness and complementary football all it wants. If the starting quarterback is living on the edge of disaster every week, the ceiling stays exactly where it is.

And that is the part people need to stop soft-selling.

Mateer is not just going through a rough stretch as an otherwise steady starter. He has been one of the least reliable full-time quarterbacks Oklahoma has put out there in a long time. You can dress it up with supporting-cast excuses if you want.

The offensive line has been shaky. The run game has been close to nonexistent. Lloyd Avant had 31 yards. The protection broke down late. All of that is fair. It is also not the whole story. Plenty of quarterbacks deal with bad line play and still avoid torpedoing their own team in the fourth quarter.

That is why the Red River game should be remembered as Mateer's best night in crimson, not proof that the job is still his without question. He rose up in a rivalry setting, and then immediately followed it by helping throw away a winnable home game against a ranked Kentucky team.

If Brent Venables and Ben Arbuckle can watch that tape and still feel comfortable saying this is the best path forward, they are seeing something the rest of us are not.

Does that mean Whitt Newbauer or Bowe Bentley is definitely the guy? No. Maybe neither one is. That is not the point.

The point is Oklahoma cannot keep running out the same answer and hoping the next opponent is the one that finally makes it look stable. At 3-3, with the season already tilting the wrong way, the Sooners owe themselves a real look at the other options.

Find out what Newbauer is. Find out what Bentley is. Stop assuming Mateer's experience automatically outweighs the turnovers, the stalled drives, and the constant sense that one bad decision is always nearby.

Sooner fans have been through enough of this version of the offense. The Texas win was fun. It was needed. It was not a free pass for every ugly tape that follows.

Oklahoma needs a spark. Right now, Mateer looks like a dead man walking under center, and the rest of the offense is stuck living with that.

The Sooners haven't seen worse quarterback play from a full-time starter since the John Blake era with Eric Moore and Brandon Daniels, all the way back in the late 1990s.

Moving on does not guarantee anything. Keeping him as the unquestioned answer guarantees more nights like Saturday, when the defense does enough, the yardage looks fine on paper, and the quarterback still finds a way to give the game back.

The John Mateer story has flipped to the last page and should be sealed shut, forever.

Oklahoma has seen that enough. It is time to try somebody else.

articles.title: BYU football team makes history in upset win over Notre Dame
articles.summary: BYU's football program made history on Saturday night.
articles.body:
No. 2 Notre Dame and No. 8 BYU played one of the day's best college football games on Saturday.

It was a fantastic game with plenty of twists and turns that came down to the final play, but BYU prevailed, 28-24.

Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr tried to throw a touchdown pass as time expired, but couldn't connect with wide receiver Jaden Greathouse. There was definitely some contact on the play, but the officials didn't throw a flag.

BYU made some cool history , winning its first-ever AP top-10 matchup.

The Cougars are now 6-0 overall and sent a message to the college football community that they are for real. They beat a national title-contending team in the Fighting Irish and are looking to not only win the Big 12, but the national championship.

Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake has done a great job with this program over the last 11 seasons, and they're likely to be in the top five of the new AP poll on Saturday. The Cougars are also one of six undefeated FBS teams.

BYU will continue its Big 12 schedule with a road matchup against UCF next Saturday before coming home to play Arizona State on Halloween. A road matchup against Utah looms after that game on Nov. 7.

This was a big win for BYU, but the program will hope that it's just the start of what could be a special season.

articles.title: Fundora stops Hadribeaj in final second, keeps undisputed title hopes alive
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Sebastian Fundora kept his pursuit of an undisputed championship on track with a second to spare.Fundora stopped Ermal Hadribeaj with a left...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — Sebastian Fundora kept his pursuit of an undisputed championship on track with a second to spare.

Fundora stopped Ermal Hadribeaj with a left hand at 2:59 of the 12th round Saturday night at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas to retain his WBC super welterweight title.

Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) had his fourth successful title defense and handed Hadribeaj (23-1-1) his first professional loss.

"It was an interesting fight," Fundora said. "I had to go back and fight on the inside and show everyone again that I can still do that. It was dramatic to knock him out at the last second. But we'll go back to the gym and fix some things."

Fundora entered the bout looking toward a chance to unify the 154-pound division, but first had to get past a stubborn mandatory challenger.

Hadribeaj attacked the body early, crouching beneath Fundora's punches and landing looping shots over the top. Fundora caught him in the second round, and Hadribeaj increasingly turned to holding to disrupt the champion's offense.

Hadribeaj lost points for holding in the third and 11th rounds. Fundora found room for uppercuts inside and applied pressure through the middle rounds before delivering the decisive left in the final second.

"I told the ref in the fourth round that I was hurting him," Fundora said. "I kept landing body shots and was looking for that special shot to get him out of there.

"I was hitting him in the rib cage the whole time with the left hand and when I went up the middle, I heard the noise that he made. So I just kept touching that and knew it would break him."

Fundora, 28, has won five straight since Brian Mendoza knocked him out in April 2023. The 6-foot-5 southpaw from Coachella, California, captured the WBC and WBO titles against Tim Tszyu in March 2024, then stopped Chordale Booker, Tszyu and Keith Thurman in successive defenses.

"I want to go for undisputed in this division," Fundora said. "We'll break either Jaron Ennis or Josh Kelly down. Just like the last guy and the guy before that. We'll keep breaking them down."

Hadribeaj, an Albanian fighter based in Miami, earned his title opportunity with a victory over previously unbeaten Bakary Samake earlier this year.

In the co-main event, Armando Resendiz (17-3) outlasted Australia's Koen Mazoudier (16-5-1) by unanimous decision in a 10-round super middleweight bout. The judges scored it 98-92, 97-93 and 97-93.

Resendiz landed punishing left hands through the middle rounds, but Mazoudier kept trading inside and rallied late. Resendiz finished strongly, sending Mazoudier stumbling backward in the final minute.

"We pulled this off because we had great preparation," Resendiz said. "This was the kind of fight that I expected. I had to change my game plan and box and move a little bit because this was a very tough fight."

Marco Romero (16-0, 14 KOs) stopped Matias Ferreira (8-4) with a crushing right hand at 1:54 of the first round in their scheduled eight-round super middleweight bout.

"He was too slow," Romero said. "His speed and experience didn't matter."

Jaime Osuna (12-0) remained unbeaten with a majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi (13-1-1) in an eight-round middleweight bout.

"It was a fight that took everything I had from beginning to end," Osuna said.

articles.title: Oh, what a night: Conner Weigman's big game helps UH outlast Oklahoma State in top-20 matchup
articles.summary: In the Cougars' most high-stakes home game in more than a decade, UH tops Oklahoma State in a shootout to take a pivotal Big 12 game.
articles.body:
Conner Weigman threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns, including two to Amare Thomas, to lead No. 20 Houston to a 35-32 win over No. 18 Oklahoma State on Saturday.

UH's defense forced two turnovers and made a fourth-down stop near the goal line as the Cougars (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) became bowl eligible with their sixth win and remained in the Big 12 race.

You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter .

After Oklahoma State pulled within 28-25 on a 66-yard touchdown catch-and-run early in the fourth quarter, the Cougars answered as Weigman led an 85-yard drive that took just two minutes.

He hooked up with Koby Young on a 48-yard touchdown to push UH's lead to 10.

Oklahoma State made one last push, pulling within 35-32 on a 8-yard touchdown catch by Justin Bowick. Mestemaker finished with 365 yards and three touchdowns.

Thomas had been quiet the last two games as defenses focused on the All-Big 12 receiver.

Thomas set up two key touchdown drives late in the second half, delivering a 51-yard catch-and-spin move to set up Trent Walker's 2-yard touchdown catch.

After Oklahoma State scored late in the third quarter, the Cougars were faced with fourth-and-2 at the Cowboys 21. Weigman found Thomas in back right corner of the end zone for a 28-17 lead.

Thomas finished with seven catches for 126 yards as UH beat a ranked opponent at home for the first time since a 24-19 win over No. 16 Kansas State in 2024.

Oklahoma State (4-2, 2-1 Big 12) managed only a field goal in the first half before Ayo Adeyi scored on a 13-yard run and Drew Mestemaker hit Wyatt Young for a 2-yard TD.

Each time the Cowboys scored, UH answered right back.

After holding the Cowboys to a field goal on their opening drive, Patrick Overmyer hauled in a 2-yard touchdown, his fifth in the last two games, and Thomas added a 7-yard TD catch for a 14-3 halftime lead.

To begin the second half, Oklahoma State marched down the field 75 yards, capped by Adeyi's run to the right side. The drive was aided by a fumble recovery by left tackle Shaun Torgeson.

Will James had an interception and had three pass breakups.

UH's defense played without three starters - nose guard De'Marion Thomas, linebacker Jaden Yates and cornerback Jalen Mayo.

This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Navarre, Pensacola Catholic and Jay claim district volleyball crowns
articles.summary: After a hectic week, three area volleyball teams brought home district titles.
articles.body:
One day later, Navarre girls volleyball head coach Sloane FitzHenry was still trying to process it.

In her first year as the Raiders head coach, even after not practicing for a week during Hurricane Isaias , Navarre brought home its first district title in a program history with a 3-1 win over Pace in the District 1-6A final.

"It's just something we talked about all season long of wanting to do," FitzHenry said in a phone interview on Oct. 16. "Especially with such a big group of seniors. They've been in the program for so long and it's something they've been wanting."

All season, the Raiders had tried building to this moment. Even when they fell short against some of the area's top teams like Gulf Breeze, Pensacola Catholic and Tate, they knew being a part of the three-team district with Pace and Crestview that they still had a great opportunity in front of them.

That was until Isaias hit Oct. 9 and Navarre was just west of the eye. FitzHenry was having flashbacks to her junior year of high school, when Hurricane Harvey hit her hometown of Houston and her house flooded with six feet of water, forcing her to live in a one bedroom apartment and attend a different high school for months.

This year, some of her players had to evacuate and almost everyone had trees fall in their yard and lost fences. Once Navarre was told it could play, FitzHenry had to make sure everyone could come back. Some kids who played Thursday still didn't have power. But everyone was excited to return

"They were just happy to be back in the gym and be with each other," FitzHenry said. "This group is so close-knit, I think no matter what happens on the outside, once we stepped into that gym, all that mattered was we were in that gym and we wanted to win."

Since Navarre couldn't practice, FitzHenry told her to team to prepare mentally. Envision what they've wanted to accomplish all season. Toughness that helped in the district final, where all three sets were battled with the Raiders winning all by a score of 25-23. A large senior class led by program mainstays like Amiyah Byrd and Eden Kemsley, finally brought home some hardware.

The reward? A long trip down I-10 awaits, as the Raiders will be the No. 8 seed in Region 1-6A and learn their opponent in the FHSAA selection show at 1 p.m. CT on Sunday. But after everything Navarre went through this week, that doesn't seem as daunting.

"We're getting to take a trip, and that's something they've really been wanting," FitzHenry said. "I'm so grateful that this is something they get to experience now and they want to play good teams. They want to play really good competition and I truly feel like that we as a team can take on anyone just by sticking together and playing our game, winning that serve and pass."

Pensacola Catholic sweeps South Walton for District 1-3A title

The Crusaders dominate the Wildcats in volleyball

Crusaders head coach Clay Carrell likes to break the season down into three parts.

Pensacola Catholic (23-4) had an excellent regular season, picking up homecourt advantage throughout the district tournament. They parlayed that into the program's first district title since 2022, sweeping Pensacola (25-9, 25-11, 25-5) in the semifinals on Oct. 16 and then South Walton (25-21, 25-20, 25-22) the next day to bring home the title.

"Proud of how my players came out ready to play," Carrell said in a text to the PNJ. "They started the sets off strong and when it got close they were able to find a way to score and push ahead."

Pensacola Catholic advanced to the 3A state semifinals last year , while South Walton (19-7) did the same in 4A before moving down a class in the most recent realignment. However, the Crusaders lost to North Bay Haven in the District 1-3A final last year before beating the Buccaneers in the Region 1-3A final.

That team finished the year 62nd in the MaxPreps state rankings, while this team currently ranks 27th in MaxPreps state rankings and 15th in the FHSAA rankings.

They'll be a top two seed in the Region 1-3A playoffs, which start Oct. 20 with the regional quarterfinals. Whether Catholic gets the top seed or not likely depends on whether Alachua Santa Fe, who entered the district tournament the top team in Region 1-3A and ninth overall in the FHSAA rankings, did enough to move into the top eight and qualify for the open division.

Top-ranked Jay repeats as Rural District 1 champions

See Jaguars take on Royals during Jay vs West Florida volleyball

After a rollercoaster week, the Lady Royals accomplished their goal.

Jay is clinched back-to-back Rural District 1 titles with a sweep of Baker (25-15, 25-15, 25-20) at Laurel Hill on Oct. 17.

"So proud of my girls," Jay head coach Carey Locklin said. "With the hurricane affecting our town so badly, with their homes damaged and no power for many days, they showed up for their town."

Coming off a 3-1 win at TR Miller, Alabama before Hurricane Isaias hit, Jay (24-2) was getting antsy to return to the court and build on that momentum. The Lady Royals were able to practice Wednesday and Thursday before going to districts, rolling with a sweep of Laurel Hill (25-8, 25-12, 25-23) in the semifinals before doing the same to Baker.

Last year was Jay's first district title in 30 years , snapping Baker's (18-5) streak of 22 straight. This year, the Lady Royals have beat the Gators in all three meetings in three different gyms, dropping just one set combined.

After advancing to the Rural Region 1 final last year, Jay will enter this year's state playoff as the No. 1 ranked team in the entire Rural classification. The Lady Royals have never advanced to the Final Four and are looking to make more history in the coming weeks, which starts with the Rural Region 1 semifinals on Oct. 24.

"We're playing really well right now and don't plan to let up," Locklin said. "Our goal is of course State, but we know what we have to do to get there. Stay focused and get one set at a time to get there.

Highlights of the Pace vs Gulf Breeze volleyball match

Dolphins head coach Steven Clay knew local teams thought this would be the year to get Gulf Breeze.

That remained true for every team in the panhandle, as the Dolphins beat all local competition except for Niceville. The Eagles ended Gulf Breeze's seven-year district title streak going on the road and beating the Dolphins 3-1 (25-23, 22-25, 25-20, 25-16) at The Tank to win the District 1-5A title.

Niceville (21-4), who had lost to Gulf Breeze (18-5) in the District 1-6A final the last two years , also won at Gulf Breeze 3-2 on Sept. 17. The two teams were supposed to play again in Okaloosa County on Oct. 8, which was cancelled due to the impending arrival of Hurricane Isaias.

The Eagles controlled the delayed rematch, with the Dolphins rallying to steal the second set but otherwise struggling to keep up.

Gulf Breeze entered the district tournament as the top seed in a tight Region 1-5A, but will have to wait for the selection show to see where it ends up seed wise. The top five teams in the region are ranked fourth through eighth overall in class 5A, with the other four besides Gulf Breeze winning their respective district tournaments. If the Dolphins match up with a district champion in the regional quarterfinals, they'd have to play on the road.

"We've always been blessed with strong players in this program," Clay said after Gulf Breeze's District 1-5A semifinal win over Milton on Oct. 16. "But this year has been unique in that it's probably the biggest hodge podge of players we've ever had. What I mean by that is historically it's always been long-term indoor players. Now, a third of the team plays indoor, a third of the team plays beach, a third of the team didn't play anything. There was no built in chemistry to start the season and I'm super proud (of) as well as they have done."

articles.title: Kentucky’s Hot Streak Rolls On At Oklahoma
articles.summary: Heading into Saturday night, Kentucky was one of the hottest teams in college football. Not only were they the winners of four straight, but they are the onl...
articles.body:
Heading into Saturday night, Kentucky was one of the hottest teams in college football. Not only were they the winners of four straight, but they are the only FBS team in history to win back-to-back one-point overtime games. In addition

Will Stein became the first coach since Alpha Brumage in 1913 to start his UK career 5-1. To keep the momentum going, they'd have to win at a place where they've never won. If they did, they'd be tied for first place in the SEC. On a night where the offense struggled, the defense had their backs. Put it all together and Kentucky's hot streak rolls on at Oklahoma 21-13.

Kentucky's Hot Streak Rolls On At Oklahoma

Heading into Saturday night's game, Oklahoma was 5-5 in stopping teams on the opening drive as every team had punted. That was until Kentucky came to town.

Taking the opening kick, the Wildcats went 67 yards in 13 plays, holding the ball for nearly seven minutes. The final two came on a pass from Kenny Minchey to Willie Rodriguez, and Kentucky led 7-0. We've said it for years, and it still holds.

Throw the ball to the tight end and good things will happen.

On their first possession, Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer led a very nice drive down the field before the Wildcat defense held. Tate Sandell picked up where he left off against Texas and was true from 46, making it 7-3.

Kentucky went quiet on their second possession, and the Sooners got another long drive. This time they got to the Wildcat 10 before Jay Bateman's group held again. After lining up for another Sandell field goal, coach Brent Venables called for the fake, which did not work. Jordan Castell picked it off in the end zone, and the lead remained 7-3.

Following another punt, Kentucky had the Sooners pinned back in their own territory at the 10. For a third straight time, OU had a drive of over 10 plays. The third time was the charm as Mateer found Rocky Beers on a 20-yard strike, and it was 10-7 Oklahoma at the half.

After getting 63 yards on their first drive, the Wildcat offense barely equaled that for the rest of the half. On the other side of the ball, Oklahoma, who struggled on third down, went 7-10 in the first half.

Not much happened for most of the third period. In fact, a Sandell 28-yard field goal was the only scoring as Oklahoma extended their lead to six. However, near the end of the quarter, Stein's Cats needed a boost as their offense struggled.

They got it from their defense as they took over.

In our game preview, we talked about how Mateer can be turnover-prone. On a 1st and 10 from the UK 38, Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace tipped a Mateer pass, and Ty Bryant was waiting, picking it off and taking it all the way to the OU 44.

Minchey marched the Cats down the field, and UK took the lead on a 12-yard strike to Rodriguez, and the Cats led 14-13.

Again, tight end play has been so instrumental to Kentucky's success this season.

Not happy with just tipping a pass, Humphrey-Grace sacked Mateer twice on the next possession. After a punt, UK drove it down to the Sooners' five-yard line. On a fourth and three, Stein went for it rather than kick a field goal. However, Minchey was sacked, and momentum seemed to shift.

Once again, the defense came up big as Kentucky's hot streak rolls on at Oklahoma.

A 58-yard punt by Wilson Berry pinned Oklahoma at their own four. Mateer got his team moving before the turnover bug hit again. Again, Castell read the throw perfectly and took it to the house for the Cats.

Trailing by eight, Mateer had one more shot, but Bryant picked him off again, and that was it as Kentucky's hot streak rolls on to 21-13 at Oklahoma.

With the win, the Wildcats go to 6-1 and 4-1 in the SEC. Not only are they bowl-eligible for the first time since 2023, but they are tied for first in the league. They've also won three straight road SEC games for the first time since 2009.

They look to keep things rolling next Saturday when they host Vanderbilt at 7:30 on the SEC Network. The Cats have lost three of the last four to the Commodores. Clark Lea's team is coming off a 31-21 home loss to Arkansas, the Razorbacks' first league win since 2024.

On the other side of the ball, the Sooners drop to 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the SEC. They travel to Mississippi State next week.

A lot of national pundits asked, "Who could be this year's Indiana?" A team coming from out of nowhere to being a national contender. Seven games into the season, Kentucky certainly looks like they fit the bill. Most likely they will move from the Reliaquest Bowl into the playoff in our next bowl projections. A team picked to finish 14th in the pre-season is now tied at the top of the SEC. It's certainly a new day in Lexington.

On a night when the offense struggled, the defense stepped up and forced three turnovers. This despite having five less first downs (19-14) and being outgained 346-230. However, what matters is the scoreboard, and the Wildcats were on the smiling side of it. Kentucky's hot streak rolls on at Oklahoma, 21-13. The Cats get their first-ever win in Norman after losing 29-7 in 1980.
